## Route contracts

- **P1 Composer:** accepted bytes/cadence; STOP only on an actual routed P1 release.
- **P2 Service 108:** one-shot cadence, feedback and protocol-specific cleanup.
- **P3 STK:** explicit numeric side; Side1 fallback one-shot with no refresh or separate P3 release.
- **P4 Pairlink:** separate frame, crypto, session, state and transport roles; no central-write substitute for local server operations.
- Shared behavior uses accepted target-specific hold, admission and card patterns. Android host retry remains excluded; HA keeps its path-aware retry policy.

## Runtime direction and current candidate

Root direction 005 resolves the credential, BlueZ mapping, and role choices. The candidate now contains a concrete entry-owned native/runtime reducer, real central notification and local `WriteValue` consumers, selected local-profile startup, per-peer auth/session routing, fixed FFD2 reads, subscription/disconnect separation, and all-target Pairlink comfort preparation. The adjacent JSON gives exact code/test refs for P4-R01..R07 and T01..T12. Every canonical implementation status remains pending root review; this is not acceptance or implementation credit.

- **D01:** Home Assistant defines UTF-8 for default text `1122` and explicit text, requiring exactly four bytes. An optional exact-four-byte hex override is validated before setup. This is HA policy, not a recovered Android charset. HomeID origin and signed LE4 normalization remain explicit; secrets stay out of representations, diagnostics, and logs.
- **D02:** BlueZ uses its daemon-managed CCCD and peer `AcquireNotify`. FFD2 remains READ|NOTIFY with fixed read value `66`; FFD1 receives protocol writes. No duplicate `2902` or artificial FFD2 WRITE flag is added. The Android descriptor callback and hidden permission split are not represented by the public BlueZ API. HA requests a 100 ms host interval and optional +1 dBm only when reported capability permits; these are host preferences, not source-phone measurements.
- **D03:** Central remains the default role. Local-host join is explicit and binds to one selected active local source. Role is independent of model selection. Runtime keys, tasks, sockets, and peer state are entry-owned. Role/auth failure never triggers silent transport fallback.

The local path keeps strict adapter, manager, permission, capacity, registration, peer-identity, and source-session checks. Real adapter grants, supported advertising slots, and concurrent-role behavior remain unobserved in fake-bus tests. Physical bed effects remain deferred to users after beta/release. See [the Reverie guide](../../beds/reverie.md).
